alternatives: Duplicate the reserved list in schemas plus an equality test
Do all alias validation in the service (loses the OpenAPI pattern and the list-style 422)
data.rationale: LinkCreate validates alias type, length and charset (StrictStr, 3-32, [A-Za-z0-9_-]), giving a FastAPI 422 list detail. LinkService rejects reserved aliases case-insensitively via codes.is_reserved, raising UnprocessableEntityError('Alias is reserved'), which gives 422. 'metrics' is added to codes.RESERVED_CODES, so generated codes and aliases share one list. — Schemas may not import app.* (architecture test), so the reserved list cannot be checked there without duplicating it. Keeping it in the service gives one source of truth (NFR-5, R6). The format check in the schema documents the pattern in OpenAPI.
data.title: ADR-1: Alias format in schema, reserved words in service with codes.RESERVED_CODES

alternatives: Skip the format check on lookup (extra DB queries for garbage paths)
data.rationale: Add codes.is_valid_lookup_code (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$) and use it in LinkService._get_or_404 and StatsService.get_stats. is_valid_code_format stays base62-only. — tests/test_codes.py asserts is_valid_code_format('abc-123') is False (R3). Lookups must accept aliases with '-'/'_'. Malformed codes still get 404 without a query. '-'/'_' codes that do not exist are now valid-but-unknown, which is still 404.
data.title: ADR-2: Separate lookup validator instead of widening CODE_PATTERN

data.rationale: If alias is given: pre-check get_by_code (friendly 409), then one LinkRepository.add. On IntegrityError: rollback. If an Idempotency-Key was sent and its record now exists, replay it or return 409. Otherwise raise ConflictError('Alias already in use'). codes.generate_code is never called on this path. The generated-code retry loop is unchanged. — Under a uniqueness race exactly one request wins and the rest get 409, never a random code or 503 (FR-3, NFR-4, R4). The unique constraint uq_links_code is the real guarantee.
data.title: ADR-3: Alias path is a single insert, and IntegrityError gives 409

alternatives: Manual SQL only (deploys break until a DBA acts)
Single DATETIME literal for all dialects (broken on PostgreSQL)
Compile the type via the dialect and format it into SQL (string-built SQL is forbidden)
data.rationale: After create_all, ensure_schema(engine) inspects links. If expires_at is missing, it executes text('ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at DATETIME NULL'). On the postgresql dialect only, it executes text('ALTER TABLE links ADD COLUMN expires_at TIMESTAMP NULL'), because PostgreSQL has no DATETIME type. Both are literal strings passed straight to text(). If the ALTER fails with DBAPIError and the column now exists, this is a tolerated concurrent race. Otherwise it logs an error and re-raises. The manual SQL is documented. No Alembic. — create_all never alters tables (R1). Literal text() keeps the static test green. SQLite and MySQL get exactly the DDL in the requirement. The postgresql branch is a deliberate, called-out deviation so that pre-CR-142 Postgres databases actually migrate: DATETIME would fail there with 'type does not exist'. TIMESTAMP is what SQLAlchemy DateTime creates on Postgres anyway. TIMESTAMP is not used everywhere because on MySQL it means TZ conversion and a 2038 limit.
data.title: ADR-4: Idempotent startup migration with literal DDL in core/db.ensure_schema

alternatives: Future check inside the schema using datetime.now (not controllable in tests)
data.rationale: LinkCreate.expires_at: dt.datetime|None with a mode='before' validator that accepts only None, datetime instances, or str matching a strict ISO-8601 date-time regex (rejects int/bool/''/'tomorrow'/date-only/unix strings). Pydantic then parses it (rejecting month 13), and a mode='after' validator normalises it with _as_utc (naive = UTC). LinkService converts to naive UTC and requires expires_at > self.now(). Otherwise it raises UnprocessableEntityError('expires_at must be in the future'). The clock is LinkService(clock=...), which deps fill from app.state.clock (None means models.utcnow, looked up at call time). — Pydantic lax mode accepts numbers and numeric strings as unix time (R9). Strict mode rejects JSON strings under FastAPI's python validation. The schema cannot reach an injectable clock, but the service can, which allows the 'equal to now gives 422' test (R5).
data.title: ADR-5: expires_at: ISO-only parsing in schema, future check in service with an injectable clock

alternatives: Always hash the new canonical payload (breaks legacy keys)
data.rationale: compute_request_hash(url, alias, expires_at_naive_utc) returns sha256(url) when alias and expires_at are both None. Otherwise it returns sha256 of json.dumps({'alias':..., 'expires_at': 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ' or None, 'url':...}, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False). The idempotency lookup runs before the reserved/future checks, so a retried successful request always replays. — Stored keys keep replaying (R2). Equal instants in different offsets hash the same. Different alias or expiry gives 409. Failed attempts store no record because the record is only added in the same transaction as a successful link insert.
data.title: ADR-6: Backwards-compatible idempotency request_hash

alternatives: SQL filter on expires_at (extra query or query change)
data.rationale: Link.is_expired_at(now) returns expires_at is not None and expires_at <= now. Redirect and HEAD check `not is_active` first (GoneError, 'Link has been deactivated'), then expiry (LinkExpiredError, 'Link has expired'), before any click insert. is_expired for responses is computed by the service and returned in CreateResult/LinkDetail. is_active is not changed by expiry. — No extra query (NFR-1). Keeps the existing deactivated 410 unchanged (FR-6, Q-3). One clock source for both redirect and metadata.
data.title: ADR-7: Expiry evaluated from the loaded row; deactivation takes precedence

data.rationale: Change @router.head('/{code}') to include_in_schema=True with responses 307/404/410, so FR-13's 410 documentation covers HEAD. — FR-13 requires HEAD to list 410. Behaviour is unchanged. Existing OpenAPI tests only assert the presence of paths and schemas.
